items.title: MCP hub: configure upstream MCP servers once and expose them to every provider
items.body:
## Problem

Every provider wraps its own MCP configuration, and hand-editing them all is the tax users pay every time they add Jira, Postgres, Notion, or any new tool server. When the user handoffs mid-task, agents lose tools the previous provider had configured. Moonfold should act as the **MCP hub**: configure an upstream MCP server once, and every provider gets it — automatically, on every handoff.

## What exists today (build on this, don't rebuild)

- Moonfold already **serves** MCP to agents: `apps/server/src/mcp/McpHttpServer.ts`, `McpSessionRegistry.ts`, toolkits under `apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/*`, with session and access-control machinery (`McpToolAccess.ts`, `threadAccess.ts`).
- Providers already connect to Moonfold's MCP surface through per-adapter wiring, so the injection point for extra tools exists.
- Server settings have a safe secret-store path (`apps/server/src/settingsSecrets.ts`) for upstream credentials, and headers/queries are redacted at logging boundaries.

## Proposal

1. Users register upstream MCP servers (stdio or HTTP transport) in server settings: name, transport, command/URL, env vars, per-tool allowlist. Secrets go through the existing secret store, never into plain settings.
2. Moonfold connects to the upstream servers (lazily, with a connection deadline) and re-exposes their tools on Moonfold's existing MCP surface, **namespaced** by server name (`jira.create_ticket`), so each provider subscribes to one host and inherits the hub.
3. Enablement is per environment or per project; tool failures are surfaced like any provider tool error and degrade the turn, not the session.
4. Per-adapter decisions must be written down for **all** adapters (Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Antigravity) per the hit-every-surface rule — e.g., tool-count caps, whether a provider truncates long tool lists, whether stdio-only upstreams can be bridged or must be proxied.
5. Handoffs need zero work: the tool surface is Moonfold's, not configured in provider CLIs. That's the core payoff.

## Acceptance criteria

- One example server (docs tool or task tool) configured once is listed and callabl by agents on at least three providers in test.
- Upstream secrets appear nowhere in prompts, briefs, or logs (assert in tests).
- Namespaced tool names survive on both web and desktop paths (they will — the surface is server-side).
- Connection failures to an upstream are typed errors agents can see, with the rest of the hub still usable.
- Concurrent tool invocations are capped; tool listings are cached cheaply.

## Non-goals

- No hosted/global proxy for other people's MCP servers; this is the user's own config, running locally.
- No marketplace/recommendation system.

## Touchpoints

- `apps/server/src/mcp/` (upstream client, hub registry, namespacing)
- `apps/server/src/serverSettings.ts` (new settings block, secrets)
- each adapter (`orchestration-v2/Adapters/*`, `provider/Drivers/*`): document only where no code is needed
- Settings UI (web + desktop)

## Contributor notes

- Maintainer-curated idea backlog. Correctness around transport bridging (stdio upstream behind HTTP host) is the hard part — sketch your design in comments or Ideas discussion before coding.

items.title: Design: `toolism proxy` — serve any MCP server's tools already slimmed
items.body:
Today users get the savings only if they run the CLI or call `slim_tools` in their own code. Most MCP users configure servers in a client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, an agent framework) and never touch the tool JSON. A proxy would give them the savings with one config change:

```json
{"command": "toolism", "args": ["proxy", "--", "npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]}
```

`toolism proxy` would start the real server over stdio, forward every message both ways, and rewrite only `tools/list` results with the safe rules.

This needs agreement on the design before code, so please discuss here first.

## Questions to settle

- **Scope of rewriting:** only `tools/list` results? Should `notifications/tools/list_changed` trigger a re-slim?
- **Safety:** safe level only, or allow `--level annotations`? Should `--verify` run once at startup, and what happens on a rollback?
- **Transport:** stdio first. Streamable HTTP later, together with #31?
- **Failure mode:** if slimming throws, pass the original tools through and log to stderr, or fail hard?
- **Observability:** one stderr line at startup with the token saving?
- **Dependencies:** lives behind the `mcp` extra; no new dependencies.
- **Testing:** an in-process fake server in `tests/servers/`, covering forwarding, pagination, `list_changed`, server crash and shutdown.

## Done when (for the design)

- [ ] The questions above are answered in this issue
- [ ] A short design note is added under `docs/design/`
- [ ] The implementation is split into one or more follow-up issues

items.title: `config --mcp-providers "core,"` saves a builtin MCP server with an empty name
items.body:
`octomind config --mcp-providers "core,"` (note the trailing comma) saves a builtin MCP server whose name is the empty string. `--mcp-providers ""` does the same, and also removes every other configured server. The command reports success either way. At runtime the blank server matches no builtin and quietly provides no tools. A blank name should be rejected with nothing saved, the way `--mcp-server` already rejects one.

Where
- `src/commands/config.rs:239` in `execute`: `let server_names: Vec<String> = providers.split(',').map(|s| s.trim().to_string()).collect();`. Empty segments are kept.
- `:240` then runs `config.mcp.servers.clear();` before anything is checked. `:243` creates `let server = McpServerConfig::builtin(server_name, DEFAULT_MCP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, Vec::new());` for each name, `""` included.
- At runtime an unknown builtin name only produces a debug log: `src/mcp/mod.rs:426-427`, `other => {` / `crate::log_debug!("Unknown builtin server: {}", other);`.
- The neighbouring flag already handles this: `src/commands/config.rs:259-264`, `if name.is_empty() {` … `block_close_err("config", "mcp server name cannot be empty");` … `return Ok(());`. It is covered by `test_mcp_server_blank_name_is_rejected`.
- Permalink: https://github.com/Muvon/octomind/blob/6ce0ded12211d64add86336d627fbfea7fedc210/src/commands/config.rs#L238-L264

Fix
- In the `--mcp-providers` branch of `execute`, check the names before `config.mcp.servers.clear()`. If any name is empty after trimming, report it with `block_open` / `block_close_err` and `return Ok(())` without saving, like the `--mcp-server` branch does.

Tests in `src/commands/config_tests.rs`, next to `test_mcp_providers_replace_servers_with_dedup`, mirroring `test_mcp_server_blank_name_is_rejected`:
- `mcp_providers = Some("core,")`, `Some("")` and `Some(" , core")` each leave no saved config (`!saved_config_path(&dir).exists()`).
- `Some("core,runtime")` still saves both servers.

Out of scope
- Rejecting names that aren't real builtins (only `core`, `runtime`, `orchestration` and `agent` exist today). That needs a decision on where the list lives, so leave it for a separate change.

New to the project? Start with CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md. Two conventions trip people up: tests go in sibling `*_tests.rs` files, and code is indented with tabs. Before opening a PR, run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`. No API key is needed. Comment here to claim the issue before opening a PR. This issue is meant for a person learning the codebase, so disclose any AI help, and don't let an agent claim or solve it. Put `Closes #<this issue>` in your PR description.

items.title: MCP initialize returns no server instructions; point the client at kb_orient

milestone.description: Follow-ups after 0.26.0: open 0.25.9 and 0.26 items that did not land by 2026-10-22.

items.body:
Split from #1286 (polish from the 2026-10-23 hallway test). A small, self-contained first issue.

**What happens.** An MCP client that connects to `pyrite mcp` gets no server `instructions` in the `initialize` result. The one hint about where to start ("Use this first") is inside the `kb_orient` tool description, one of 66 to 106 tools. Clients that show server instructions to the model (most do) show nothing. Reproduced on `dev` at d66c4555 with the Python `mcp` client:

```python
init = await session.initialize()
init.instructions        # -> None
```

**What to change.** `PyriteMCPServer.build_sdk_server` in `pyrite/server/mcp_server.py` builds the SDK server with `Server(f"pyrite-{self.tier}")` (about line 2829). The installed SDK's `Server.__init__` takes `instructions=`. Pass a short text. It should say:
- call `kb_orient` first: with no arguments it lists the KBs you can read and the operational contracts; with `kb_name` it describes one KB;
- the tier this server runs at (`self.tier`), and that tools of a higher tier are not listed;
- errors come back as a result with `error`, `error_code`, `retryable` (see `kb_orient`).

Keep it under about 600 characters. Keep the text in one constant, and do not repeat the tool descriptions.

**Acceptance.**
- A test starts the server over stdio, or builds it through `build_sdk_server`, and asserts that the `initialize` result has `instructions` naming `kb_orient` and the tier. It fails today. `tests/test_mcp_read_scoping.py` already does a real `initialize` round trip; model the test on it.
- The text is the same for every tier apart from the tier name. It is built once per connection, like the rest of the server.

**Files.** `pyrite/server/mcp_server.py` and one test. About 15 lines plus the test.

**Out of scope.** The tool descriptions themselves. `kb_link` needing `source_kb` is already in its `required` list. A tool above the connected tier answering `UNKNOWN_TOOL` is #1276.


---
_Filed by the maintainer's architect agent (automated), 2026-10-23._

---

## Groom 2026-10-23

*Automated groom (architect agent). Checked on `dev` at 3f73c653. No open PR covers this issue now: PR #1296 carried an earlier version of it and has since been cut down to #1290.*

small: 2 and 3 only

### 2. What the code does today
- `PyriteMCPServer.build_sdk_server` (`pyrite/server/mcp_server.py`, the `Server(f"pyrite-{self.tier}")` call at line 2829) passes no `instructions`. The installed SDK's `Server.__init__` takes `instructions: str | None` (checked with `inspect.signature`).
- **One place for both transports.** Stdio (`main`, about line 2942) and HTTP MCP (`pyrite/server/mcp_routes.py`, about line 379, one `PyriteMCPServer` per tier) both build through `build_sdk_server`. The text set there reaches every client.

### 3. Invariant and surfaces
**Invariant:** every MCP connection's `initialize` result tells the client where to start (`kb_orient`), which tier it is connected at, and the error shape. The text comes from one constant.

**Shapes:** tiers `read`, `write` and `admin`; transports stdio and HTTP; a client that ignores `instructions` (no change for it).

**Surfaces:** MCP only. The tool list and the descriptions stay unchanged. The characterization goldens for `initialize`, if any capture it, change on purpose; say so in the PR.

```
Acceptance:   as above, parametrised over the three tiers on stdio, and one HTTP round trip; fails today (instructions is None)
Regimes:      text length (keep it under about 600 characters; assert it)
Touches:      existing: pyrite/server/mcp_server.py   new: tests/test_mcp_initialize_instructions.py
Sequence:     independent
Model:        sonnet
heavy:        no
Cold read:    no
Out of scope: tool descriptions; a tool above the tier answering UNKNOWN_TOOL (#1276); kb_timeline's kb_name (#1233)
Decision:     none
```

**good first issue: kept.**

items.title: No MCP tool builds embeddings, so semantic search is a dead end for an MCP-only agent

milestone.description: Follow-ups after 0.26.0: open 0.25.9 and 0.26 items that did not land by 2026-10-22.

items.body:
**What happens.** An agent that works only over MCP (a Desktop-style client) cannot get semantic search.

```
kb_search {"query":"who signed off the spending paper","kb_name":"scratch-a","mode":"semantic"}
-> 0 results, warnings:["semantic leg skipped: no embeddings exist ... run `pyrite index embed` to build them"]
```
The warning is clear and honest, but no MCP tool builds embeddings. `kb_index_sync` (admin) does not, and no tool name contains "embed". The agent is stuck until a human runs the CLI. Semantic ranking was not tested.

**Expected.** An admin-tier tool (`kb_index_embed`, or an `embed` flag on `kb_index_sync`) that builds embeddings, reports progress and the model fetch, and a warning that names that tool when the caller is on MCP.

**Minimal repro.** `pyrite init -t research ...`, `pyrite mcp --tier admin`, create entries, `kb_search` with `mode:"semantic"`.

**Shapes this must hold for.** MCP `kb_search` warnings and the new tool; CLI `index embed` (human text only, no `--format json`); REST index route; the warning text must name the surface the caller is on. Test: via MCP only, create, embed, semantic search returns hits with `similarity`.

Source: `feedback/2026-10-23-hallway-mcp-memory-agent.md` Friction 5.



---

## Groom 2026-10-23

*Automated groom (architect agent). Reproduced on `dev` at d66c4555 in a scratch HOME. No open PR.*

**Principle 8, and a promise ADR-0035 already makes.** ADR-0035 decision 3 says draining the embed queue "gives the server, MCP and one-shot CLI paths the same answer instead of three". Today there are three answers, and MCP's is "never". So this is not a design gap. The design is written down; MCP was left out of it.

**The user's model.** "I wrote entries over MCP and asked for semantic search. The warning tells me what to run, and I can run it from where I am." **The implementation model.** Every write queues its embedding (`embed_queue`). A sync on any surface settles the queue through one function. The warning names a remedy the caller can reach.

### 1. Contracts that apply
- ADR-0035 (`kb/adrs/0035-writes-are-eventually-embedded-...md`), decisions 2 and 3: the queue drains on sync, and every surface gives the same answer. No new background thread.
- `kb/maps/search-and-embeddings.md`, "The design today" item 3: its list of drain points names the CLI and REST only. Add MCP when this lands.
- `docs/json-contracts.md`, "Search result envelope": `warnings` is the channel.

### 2. What the code does today
- **Reproduced.** Over MCP (admin tier): `kb_create` ×3 in a research KB, then `kb_search {"mode":"semantic"}` → 0 results, with the warning `run \`pyrite index embed\``. There are 106 tools and none has "embed" in its name. The index's `embed_queue` table holds a `pending` row for every MCP-created entry: the debt is recorded, and nothing on MCP pays it.
- **Three sync implementations.**
  - CLI `index_sync` (`pyrite/cli/index_commands.py`, about line 205): `sync_incremental`, then `_settle_embed_queue`, then `embed_all` when files changed (unless `--no-embed`).
  - REST `sync_index` (`pyrite/server/endpoints/admin.py`, about line 76): with `wait=true` it syncs and drains the queue (`_drain_embed_queue`). It does not embed changed files. The background branch drains nothing, on purpose (see its comment).
  - MCP `_kb_index_sync` (`pyrite/server/mcp_server.py`, about line 1927): `sync_incremental` only. `background=true` submits the `IndexWorker` thread job, which does not drain either.
- The warning is built in `SearchService._semantic_search` (`pyrite/services/search_service.py`, about line 1111). It names only the CLI command.

### 3. Invariant and surfaces
**A synchronous sync on any surface settles the embed queue, and embeds the entries it found changed on disk, through one function. The "no embeddings" warning names a remedy on every surface.**

| Surface | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| CLI `index sync` | sync + settle + embed changed | calls the shared function |
| CLI `index build`, `index embed`, `pyrite-admin index embed` | settle + embed all | unchanged (embed is a different verb) |
| REST `POST /api/index/sync?wait=true` | sync + settle | shared function (now also embeds changed files) |
| REST background sync | sync only | unchanged (nobody is waiting) |
| MCP `kb_index_sync` | sync only | shared function; the result gains `embedded`, `pending` and, when skipped, `embedding_skipped` with the reason |
| MCP `kb_index_sync background=true` | thread job, sync only | unchanged, and its description says so |

**Shapes** (each a row of the acceptance test):
- `auto_embed: true`, rows queued by MCP writes: settled, and `semantic` search then returns rows with `similarity`.
- `auto_embed: false`: nothing is queued, and sync embeds nothing. The warning must not tell this user to embed: check what `_semantic_search` says today in this case.
- Files added or edited by hand, then synced: embedded (CLI does this today; REST and MCP do not).
- The semantic extra is not installed: sync still succeeds and reports `embedding_skipped: "dependency_missing"` with the install hint. It does not refuse.
- The model cannot be fetched (offline): the rows stay `pending`, the result says how many, and the sync succeeds.
- The first run downloads the model (~90 MB, about 10 s in the hallway run on a fast link).

### 4. Options
- **A (recommended).** One function, for example `sync_and_settle(index_mgr, kb_name, embed=True) -> dict` in `pyrite/services/embedding_worker.py` beside `settle_embed_queue`. The CLI, REST (`wait=true`) and MCP call it. The warning text names both remedies in one place: "run `pyrite index embed` (CLI) or `kb_index_sync` (MCP, admin tier)".
- **B.** A new admin tool `kb_index_embed` that mirrors `index embed` (with `force`). This gives MCP the "re-embed everything" verb too. It can follow A; it does not replace A, because A is the ADR's promise.
- **C.** Drain at MCP server start, as REST does. Rejected: it loads torch in every stdio session start, and ADR-0035 kept that cost on the server's prewarm.

### 5. Open questions
- MCP clients time out long calls (Desktop clients differ). A first sync that downloads the model may exceed the timeout. Measure it. If it is a problem, bound the drain (a batch per call, `pending` reported, call again), rather than moving the drain to the background thread (#102's hazard, which ADR-0035 refuses to copy).
- REST `wait=true` starting to embed changed files is a behaviour change. Name it in the changelog, or leave REST out of the "embed changed" half and say why.

### 6. Pointers
`settle_embed_queue` / `settle_embed_queue_by_kb` (`pyrite/services/embedding_worker.py`); `_embed_counts` in `index_commands.py`; tests `tests/test_embedding_queue.py`, `tests/test_embed_queue_debt_is_honest.py`, `tests/test_semantic_search_warns_when_nothing_is_embedded.py`, `tests/test_server_write_embedding_debt.py`.

### 7. Checked versus assumed
Ran: the MCP reproduction, the queue table, all three sync paths read. Assumed: the fakes in the queue tests let the new test run without the real model (true of `test_embedding_queue.py` as far as I read it). Checked: `pyrite/storage/index.py` never mentions the queue or embedding, so a sync does not enqueue hand-edited files, and the "embed changed" half is needed. **This groom is wrong if** a plugin hook or `KBService` path enqueues on sync that I did not find. Then the shared function is just sync + settle.

```
Acceptance:   via MCP only (admin tier): create 2 entries, kb_index_sync, kb_search mode=semantic returns hits with
              similarity (fails today); parametrised over the shapes above on CLI, REST wait=true and MCP; the warning
              names kb_index_sync. A test fails if a sync path calls sync_incremental without the shared function
              (grep-style guard over pyrite/cli, pyrite/server).
Regimes:      the shapes list; background=true unchanged and documented.
Touches:      existing: pyrite/services/embedding_worker.py, pyrite/cli/index_commands.py, pyrite/server/endpoints/admin.py,
              pyrite/server/mcp_server.py, pyrite/server/tool_schemas.py (kb_index_sync description),
              pyrite/services/search_service.py (warning), kb/maps/search-and-embeddings.md, docs/json-contracts.md (result keys)
              new: tests/test_sync_settles_embed_queue_everywhere.py.  About 9 files, +220/-60.
Sequence:     independent.
Model:        opus
heavy:        no (use the queue tests' fakes; no model download in CI)
Cold read:    yes (a public MCP result shape and a REST behaviour change)
Out of scope: kb_index_embed (option B, a follow-up); semantic ranking quality (not tested in the report).
Decision:     none needed (ADR-0035 decides it). Option B is the maintainer's call if wanted.
```

`good first issue`: not added (three surfaces, an ADR, a behaviour change).

items.title: One way to name the KB: -k/--kb on every CLI command and kb_name on every MCP tool

milestone.description: Follow-ups after 0.26.0: open 0.25.9 and 0.26 items that did not land by 2026-10-22.

items.body:
**What happens.** The same job, naming the KB, is spelled differently across commands and tools, and guessing wrong costs a round trip.

CLI:
```
pyrite qa validate -k proj        -> Error: No such option: -k   (correct: pyrite qa validate proj)
pyrite qa stale|status|gaps|assess -k proj   -> same
pyrite qa checkers proj           -> unexpected extra argument   (this one takes --kb/-k)
pyrite ci -k reading-kb           -> No such option: -k          (correct: ci --kb)
pyrite kb validate reading-kb     (positional)   ; pyrite kb health reading-kb -> Missing option '--kb' / '-k'
pyrite index sync                 (no KB at all) ; pyrite index health -k
pyrite create (no -k)             -> VALIDATION_FAILED: --kb is required ; update/backlinks -> USAGE_ERROR: Missing option
```
`qa` mixes both conventions inside one group. Defaults also differ inside `qa`: `stale` and `checkers` print rich tables, `validate` and `status` print JSON, `gaps` prints text with no `--format`.

MCP: `kb_get`, `kb_create`, `kb_recent` take `kb_name`; `kb_registry_health` takes `name`; `kb_commit` takes `kb`. Guessing `kb_name` gives a schema error (`'name' is a required property`) as isError:true, while every other error is a normal result with an `error` key, so a client must check both.

**Expected.** Every command accepts `-k/--kb` (a positional KB stays as an alias); MCP tools take `kb_name` (old names accepted as aliases for a deprecation window); a missing KB gives one error code. Usage errors suggest the accepted spelling, not only "Try --help".

**Minimal repro.** Commands above.

**Shapes this must hold for.** Every CLI group (`qa`, `kb`, `index`, `ci`, `links`, `sw`, `task`, `export`, `timeline`), every MCP tool schema (assert in a test that no tool names its KB parameter anything but `kb_name`), REST query parameters. Related: #947 (`-f` ambiguity), #610 (No such KB spellings).

Source: CLI research Friction 5 and 9, CLI software Friction 2, MCP Friction 8 (`feedback/2026-10-23-hallway-*.md`).



## Groom 2026-10-23

*Automated groom (architect agent). Reproduced on `dev` at `d66c4555` with a scratch `HOME`; anchors checked against `376d21d2`.*

**Principle at stake: 9** (a small supported surface that works as documented). `docs/json-contracts.md:218` already states the spellings: "`-k`, REST `kb` and MCP `kb_name` take the full name". The commands that do otherwise are the defect. Principle 8 applies to the fix: one shared way to accept the KB, not a hand-written option in each command.

**The user's model.** "I name the KB the same way everywhere: `-k` on the CLI, `kb_name` over MCP."
**The implementation model.** Every CLI command that acts on one existing KB accepts `-k/--kb`. A positional KB stays as an alias, and naming two different KBs is a usage error. Every MCP tool that acts on one existing KB takes `kb_name`. The old names are accepted as aliases until a named release. REST keeps `kb`, as documented.

### 2. What the code does today (reproduced)

- `qa validate -k rk`, `ci -k rk` and `index reconcile -k rk` give `USAGE_ERROR: No such option: -k`. `kb health rk` gives `Missing option '--kb' / '-k'`.
- `create` with no KB gives `VALIDATION_FAILED: --kb is required (unless using --template)`, while `update` and `backlinks` give `USAGE_ERROR: Missing option '--kb' / '-k'`.
- MCP `kb_registry_health {"kb_name": ...}` gives `isError: true`, "Input validation error: 'name' is a required property". The MCP SDK raises this before Pyrite's dispatcher (`@sdk.call_tool()` in `build_sdk_server`, `pyrite/server/mcp_server.py:2849`, validates input by default). Every other error is a normal result with `error_code`.

### 3. Invariant and surfaces

**Enumeration source, CLI:** the Typer command tree (`pyrite.cli.app`), walked with click. There are 156 leaf commands:

- **About 104 already take `-k/--kb`.** They are safe.
- **24 name no KB** (`auth *`, `config`, `mcp`, `serve`, `db *`, `kb list`, `kb discover`, `kb gc`, `index stats`, `index jobs`, `list`, `batch-read`, `protocol list`, ...). Safe: they are not about one KB.
- **14 take the KB as a positional only (guarded by this ticket):**
  - `qa validate`, `qa status`, `qa assess`, `qa stale`, `qa compact`, `qa check-urls`, `qa coverage` (`pyrite/cli/qa_commands.py:27, :265, :117, :713, :768, :833, :919`)
  - `kb validate`, `kb schema show`, `kb schema set`, `kb schema add-type`, `kb schema remove-type` (`pyrite/cli/kb_commands.py:258, :655, :711, :761, :797`)
  - `index reconcile` (`index_commands.py:822`)
  - `task migrate-relaxed-mode` (`task_commands.py:559`)
- **1 takes `--kb` without `-k`:** `ci` (`pyrite/cli/__init__.py:264`). Guarded.
- **Out of scope, with reasons.** `init --name`, `kb add --name`, `kb create --name`, `kb remove <name>`: the KB is the object being created or removed, not the scope, so they stay as they are. `repo *` and `extension *` name repos and extensions. `investigation dedup/search -k` already use `-k` (repeatable).

**Enumeration source, MCP:** `list_tools` at the admin tier, 106 tools. 88 use `kb_name`, 6 name no KB, and the multi-KB tools use `source_kb`/`target_kb`/`kb_names`/`kb_a`/`kb_b`, which are correct because they name two KBs. To align:
- `kb_commit` and `kb_push` (`kb`; `_kb_commit` :2036, `_kb_push` :2053)
- `kb_registry_remove`, `kb_registry_reindex`, `kb_registry_health` (`name`; :2086, :2099, :2110)
- **Not** `kb_registry_add`: its `name` is the KB being created, the counterpart of `kb add --name`.

**Trap, read before the MCP theme.** The dispatcher finds the KBs a call names only under `KB_ARGUMENT_NAMES` (`mcp_server.py:357`: `kb_name`, `kb`, `source_kb`, ...; `name` is not among them) and refuses an unknown KB before the handler runs. Renaming a parameter to `kb_name` therefore changes which calls are checked. That is right for remove, reindex and health. It would break `kb_registry_add`: an unknown KB is refused, and that is exactly the case add exists for.

**Shapes:**
- CLI: `-k X`; `--kb X`; positional `X`; positional and `-k` the same (fine); positional and `-k` different (`USAGE_ERROR`); neither, on a command whose KB is optional (all KBs, as today); neither, on one that needs a KB.
- MCP: `kb_name`; the old name; both, differing (`VALIDATION_FAILED`); neither.

### 4. Options

- **A (recommended).** One helper in `pyrite/cli/context.py`: a `kb_option()` with a positional alias and `resolve_kb(positional, option)` that raises the usage error. Then each group in turn.
- **B.** Turn the positionals into options with no alias. This is a breaking CLI change, and docs and scripts use the positional form (`pyrite qa validate <kb>` appears in docs/). Not without a deprecation.

### Themes (take one per PR)

**Theme 1: `qa` group and the shared helper.** A good first change.
```
Acceptance:   each of the 7 qa commands accepts -k/--kb and its positional; the shapes above; --help shows both.
              Fails today: qa validate -k rk → No such option: -k.
Touches:      pyrite/cli/context.py (helper), pyrite/cli/qa_commands.py, tests/test_kb_flag_everywhere.py (new, a
              table over the command tree that fails when a command naming one KB lacks -k)
Sequence:     first. Open PRs #1243, #1240 and #1132 edit qa_commands.py in other hunks; rebase.
Model:        sonnet   heavy: no   Cold read: no
```
**Theme 2: `kb validate`, `kb schema *`, `index reconcile`, `task migrate-relaxed-mode`, `ci -k`.**
```
Acceptance:   the same shapes on these 9 commands; the tree test from theme 1 passes with no exceptions left
              except the listed out-of-scope ones
Touches:      pyrite/cli/kb_commands.py, pyrite/cli/index_commands.py, pyrite/cli/task_commands.py,
              pyrite/cli/__init__.py (ci_command)
Sequence:     after theme 1 (helper, test); #1269 edits kb_validate (another hunk)
Model:        sonnet   heavy: no   Cold read: no
```
**Theme 3: MCP `kb_name` on the 5 tools.**
```
Acceptance:   kb_commit, kb_push, kb_registry_remove/reindex/health take kb_name; the old name still works and
              its result carries a deprecation warning naming the removal release; a test over list_tools
              asserts every single-KB tool names it kb_name (allowlist: kb_registry_add and the multi-KB
              parameters). Fails today: kb_registry_health {kb_name} → Input validation error.
Regimes:      the dispatch KB check (above); kb_registry_add unchanged
Touches:      pyrite/server/tool_schemas.py, pyrite/server/mcp_server.py (the 5 handlers), docs/json-contracts.md
Sequence:     independent of 1-2; after theme 4 if aliases need `required` relaxed in the schema
Model:        opus   heavy: no   Cold read: yes (changes which calls the dispatch KB check sees)
```
**Theme 4: input-schema errors in the documented shape.**
```
Acceptance:   a call missing a required parameter or of the wrong type returns a result with error_code
              VALIDATION_FAILED (isError false), as every other refusal does
Touches:      pyrite/server/mcp_server.py (build_sdk_server: call_tool(validate_input=False), validate in
              _dispatch_tool), tests
Sequence:     independent; #1276 also edits _dispatch_tool's opening lines, so land one, then rebase
Model:        sonnet   heavy: no   Cold read: yes (the dispatch chokepoint)
```

### 5. Open questions

- A missing KB: should it be one code everywhere? `json-contracts.md:218` makes a *blank* name `VALIDATION_FAILED`. An *absent* required option is Click's `USAGE_ERROR`. `create` is the outlier only because `--template` makes `-k` optional. Recommend leaving it as is and documenting "absent → USAGE_ERROR, blank → VALIDATION_FAILED".
- The default output formats inside `qa` (rich vs JSON vs text) are a separate inconsistency. File it; do not fold it in.

**Out of scope:** REST parameter names (documented as `kb`); #947 (`-f` ambiguity); #610 (the spellings of "No such KB").
**Decision:** the release in which the MCP aliases (`kb`, `name`) stop being accepted. Recommend 0.28.0, named in the deprecation warning and the changelog.

**Checked versus assumed.** I walked the command tree and `list_tools` in a scratch `HOME`. I did not check whether docs/ teach the positional form for every one of the 14 commands; grep before theme 2. **This groom is wrong if** a positional KB on `qa`/`kb` is meant to be the canonical form (no doc says so). Footprint: 6-7 CLI files plus a tree test (themes 1-2, ~250 lines); 2 server files and docs (themes 3-4, ~200 lines).

items.title: feat(nodes): add a Manufact MCP Client preset of tool_mcp_client
items.body:
### Problem Statement

Manufact is on RocketRide's GTM list. It is the company behind `mcp-use` (an MCP server and client framework) and Manufact Cloud, which hosts MCP servers and exposes a management API and a management MCP server. There is no vendor REST API that a tool node would wrap in the usual way, and the generic `tool_mcp_client` can already connect to any MCP server, so an agent can use a Manufact-hosted server today by typing its URL. Nothing in the canvas carries Manufact's name or logo, which is the go-to-market gap.

The repo already has the right shape for this case. `nodes/src/nodes/tool_mcp_client/services.butterbase.json` is a branded "Butterbase MCP Client" preset of the generic MCP client: its own protocol (`tool_butterbase://`), title, logo, default endpoint and API-key field, sharing the implementation in `nodes.tool_mcp_client`. A Manufact preset does the same.

### Proposed Solution

Add `nodes/src/nodes/tool_mcp_client/services.manufact.json`, mirroring `services.butterbase.json` field for field:

- `title`: "Manufact MCP Client"; `protocol`: `tool_manufact://`; `prefix`: `manufact`; `icon`: `manufact.svg`; `path`: `nodes.tool_mcp_client`; classType `["tool"]`; `lanes: {}`.
- `description`: connects to Manufact's management MCP server, or to any MCP server you deployed on Manufact Cloud, and exposes its tools to agents as `manufact.<tool>`.
- `preconfig` profile `manufact`: `serverName: "manufact"`, `transport: "streamable-http"`, `endpoint: "https://mcp.manufact.com/mcp"`.
- `fields`: `mcp_client.bearer` (API key, secret, `ApiKeyWidget`; created at Manufact dashboard > API keys, prefixed `mcp_`, shown once, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`), `mcp_client.endpoint` (default the management server; set it to your deployed server's URL to use that server's tools), `mcp_client.serverName`.
- `shape`: one "Pipe" section with those three fields, as Butterbase has.

Two uses, one preset:

1. Management: with the default endpoint and an `mcp_` key, an agent gets Manufact's own tools: list servers, trigger a deployment, redeploy, stop a deployment, read runtime logs (tool names from https://docs.manufact.com/mcp and https://docs.manufact.com/llms.txt). This is the use with a vendor-specific value.
2. A hosted server: set `endpoint` to the deployed server's URL and the agent gets that server's tools under the same `manufact.` prefix.

API basis (https://docs.manufact.com, https://docs.mcp-use.com, https://manufact.com/openapi.json):

- Deployed-server URL: the dashboard docs give `https://<slug>.run.mcp-use.com/mcp` and preview deployments `https://<slug>--br-<branch>.run.mcp-use.com/mcp`; the mcp-use deployment page gives `https://<slug>.deploy.mcp-use.com/mcp`. The two official pages conflict; the README should tell users to copy the URL from the Manufact dashboard rather than construct it.
- Transport: the docs say only "MCP over HTTP". `tool_mcp_client` supports Streamable HTTP and legacy SSE, so the preset defaults to `streamable-http` and the README says to switch to SSE if a server answers with an SSE stream.
- Auth: `mcp_` API keys are documented for the REST API, CI and scripts (`Authorization: Bearer mcp_...`; the docs also mention `x-api-key`). Whether the management MCP server and deployed servers accept the same bearer key is not stated; the docs say a server that requires OAuth sends clients through the standard MCP OAuth flow, which `tool_mcp_client` cannot complete non-interactively.
- Management REST API: `https://cloud.manufact.com/api/v1`, bearer auth, with servers, deployments, logs and env-variable endpoints (OpenAPI 3.1 at `manufact.com/openapi.json`). This is the fallback if the management MCP needs OAuth: a small `tool_manufact` REST node with the same five operations.
- Free plan: $0, $5 monthly credits, 2 projects, 30,000 requests a month (tool calls count, discovery calls do not), 1 team member.
- Python: `mcp-use` 1.7.1 requires Python 3.11; not needed, since the preset reuses `tool_mcp_client`'s own client.

Implementation notes:

- Files: `services.manufact.json`, `manufact.svg`, a section in `tool_mcp_client/README.md` describing the preset the way the Butterbase preset is described, a credentials stub for `mcp_client.bearer` under the new protocol in `packages/ai/src/ai/modules/mcp/credentials.json`, and a `CHANGELOG.md` line. No Python changes.
- The contract tests auto-discover every `services*.json`, so the new preset is covered for title, protocol, loader and lanes with no new test code.
- Live verification: a free Manufact account, one deployed example server (Manufact deploys from a GitHub organization on the Free plan), then: (a) the default endpoint with an `mcp_` key, list tools; (b) the deployed server's URL, list and call one tool. Record both in the PR, including which hostname pattern the dashboard actually showed.
- Logo: no brand or press page exists on manufact.com (both return 404). Ask Manufact for an SVG through the partner contact; until then the preset ships with a placeholder and the PR notes it.
- Test ladder: `./builder nodes:test --pytest-pattern=mcp_client`, `python3 scripts/validate-node-readme.py nodes/src/nodes/tool_mcp_client`.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] "Manufact MCP Client" appears in the canvas with its own icon and the three fields
- [ ] With an `mcp_` key and the default endpoint, an agent lists Manufact's management tools and reads a deployment's logs, recorded in the PR; or, if the management server requires OAuth, the PR says so and the default endpoint is changed to empty with the README pointing at hosted servers only
- [ ] With a deployed server's URL, an agent lists and calls that server's tools as `manufact.<tool>`
- [ ] Contract tests pass; README validator passes; credentials stub present; CHANGELOG line; `CI OK` green

Size estimate: about 80 lines of JSON plus a README section and the icon; 1 to 2 person-days including the live verification.

Open questions:

- Does `https://mcp.manufact.com/mcp` accept an `mcp_` key as a bearer token, or does it require the MCP OAuth flow? This decides whether the management use works from a pipeline. If OAuth only, file the `tool_manufact` REST fallback described above.
- Which hostname pattern a given deployed server uses (`*.run.mcp-use.com` or `*.deploy.mcp-use.com`).
- An official SVG logo.

### Alternatives Considered

- The generic `tool_mcp_client` with a typed URL: works today, carries no Manufact branding, and leaves users to find the endpoint and auth details themselves.
- A `tool_manufact` REST node over `cloud.manufact.com/api/v1`: the fallback if the management MCP needs OAuth; otherwise it duplicates what the MCP server already exposes.

### Affected Modules

- [ ] server (C++ engine)
- [ ] client-typescript
- [ ] client-python
- [ ] client-mcp
- [x] nodes (pipeline)
- [x] ai (credentials catalog)
- [ ] vscode

Good first contribution for a partner engineer (see epic #1522; part of the GTM node integrations epic, #2798). Template: `tool_mcp_client/services.butterbase.json`.

items.title: Expose team search as an MCP tool
items.body:
Coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, others) could search a team's documents through an MCP server that exposes one tool, for example `search_team(query, k)`, backed by the local `POST /search` endpoint of `potluckrag share`.

**Important:** the passages would then go to the agent's model provider, which is usually a cloud API. That changes the README's "Data sent" table, so the tool must be opt-in, and the docs must say this plainly.

**What to build**

- A `potluckrag mcp` command that runs an MCP server over stdio and calls the local endpoint.
- The tool returns passages with their `member:path#Lstart-end` labels.
- No new runtime dependency unless discussed here first (the MCP stdio protocol is small enough to implement directly).

items.title: tdrive mcp add on Windows (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor)
items.body:
## What

`tdrive mcp add claude|codex|cursor` sets up an AI client on a person's own computer. It works on macOS (Keychain) and Linux (0600 token file). On **Windows** it doesn't work yet: the generated `headersHelper` uses POSIX shell (`"$(cat …)"`), and the config paths assume a Unix home directory.

Many people on small teams use Windows laptops with the Codex app, Claude Code or Cursor, so this matters even though the *server* stays macOS/Linux.

## Pointers

- `src/client/mcp.ts`: `clientPaths()`, the store choice (`keychain` / `file` / `inline`), `helperGet`.
- Windows options for the token: the Windows Credential Manager (e.g. via PowerShell `Get-StoredCredential` or `cmdkey`), or a file with an ACL limited to the user.
- Codex uses `bearer_token_env_var`, Cursor `${env:…}`: check how each expects env vars on Windows.

## Done when

- [ ] `tdrive mcp add …` works on Windows 11 for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, token stored outside the client config.
- [ ] `--dry-run` output is correct on Windows; tests cover the Windows branch with `platform: 'win32'`.
- [ ] `docs/CONNECT-CLIENTS.md` has a Windows section.

items.title: MCP approval tests bind approval and nonce lifetimes to the wall clock

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: Rust code or tests; needs the gate suite; the issue states the design

labels.name: agent-ready
labels.description: Where and Acceptance are commands; a coding agent can take it; Gates only beyond preflight

items.body:
Six MCP integration tests create approval rules, approval entries, or nonces whose lifetimes start at the wall clock: 60 seconds for the nonces and entries, 120 seconds for the rules. When a run is slow, for example while another test suite runs on the same machine, the time between a fixture and its commit can cross a lifetime. The test then fails with an expiry code instead of the outcome it checks.

Where (line numbers at ef96faf):

- `crates/stellar-agent-mcp/tests/mcp/approval_consumed_integration.rs`: the policy double's rule lifetime is 120 seconds (`:69-72`), and the commit nonces expire 60 seconds after the wall clock (`:335-336`, `:571-572`, `:767-768`). The tests at `:231`, `:238`, `:490`, and `:641` need the rule and the nonce still valid at their first or only commit. The second commit of the first two tests answers from the receipt before any expiry check.
- `crates/stellar-agent-mcp/tests/mcp/approval_attestation_indistinguishability.rs`: the rule lifetime is 120 seconds (`:145-148`), and the approval entries live 60 seconds (`:846`, `:965`). The tests at `:792` and `:915` need the entry still valid at the gate. The first expects the signer refusal behind the gate, and the second expects the owner-key warning that key loading emits.

Current behavior at ef96faf, reproduced by inserting `tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(N)).await;`:

- 61 seconds before the first commit (`approval_consumed_integration.rs:353`): both tests at `:231` and `:238` fail at `:373` with `nonce.expired`.
- 130 seconds at the same place: both fail at `:373` with `policy.approval_required`, because the rule has expired.
- 61 seconds before the commits at `approval_attestation_indistinguishability.rs:871` and `:985`: both tests fail, because the gate answers with the uniform approval error before the step each test checks.
- 130 seconds before the second commit (`approval_consumed_integration.rs:412`): both tests pass.

Expected: the six tests pass with a delay of 130 seconds before any of their commits. The tests keep their assertions, and no production code changes.

- The rule lifetimes at `approval_consumed_integration.rs:71` and `approval_attestation_indistinguishability.rs:147` become 86,400 seconds, the production default (`DEFAULT_APPROVAL_TTL_SECONDS` in `crates/stellar-agent-core/src/policy/v1/loader.rs:99`).
- The entry lifetimes at `approval_attestation_indistinguishability.rs:846` and `:965` become `DEFAULT_TTL_MS` (`crates/stellar-agent-core/src/approval/store.rs:128`).
- The nonces get a distant expiry and a mint time derived from it, for example `expiry = u64::MAX` and `now_ms = expiry - 60_000`. The nonce crate takes both as parameters (`crates/stellar-agent-nonce/src/mint.rs:522`, `:785`). The second mint at `approval_consumed_integration.rs:401-406` passes `now_ms + 1`, which still leaves a valid lifetime. The scaffold nonce at `approval_attestation_indistinguishability.rs:259-260` gets the same treatment: its fixed 2030 epoch stops verifying after 2030-01-01T00:01:00Z.
- Tests that check an expired approval on purpose, such as `rule_ttl_bounds_toolset_queued_approval_at_commit` (`approval_cap_integration.rs:1025`) and `property4c_expired_approval_entry_returns_approval_required`, stay as they are.

Acceptance:

```bash
grep -nE 'let expiry = now_ms \+ 60_000;|^[[:space:]]+(120|60_000),' crates/stellar-agent-mcp/tests/mcp/approval_consumed_integration.rs crates/stellar-agent-mcp/tests/mcp/approval_attestation_indistinguishability.rs | wc -l   # prints 0 (7 at ef96faf)
cargo test -p stellar-agent-mcp --features test-helpers --test mcp approval_consumed_integration
cargo test -p stellar-agent-mcp --features test-helpers --test mcp approval_attestation_indistinguishability
cargo test -p stellar-agent-mcp --features test-helpers --test mcp
```

Each run ends with `test result: ok`. Then insert the delays from "Current behavior" one at a time, using 130 seconds everywhere: every listed test passes. Remove the sleeps afterwards.

Hints: `tokio::time::pause` does not help, because the lifetimes are read from the wall clock (`crates/stellar-agent-core/src/timefmt.rs:24`). The tests are already `#[serial]`, which does not stop the wall clock or the delay another process causes.

To claim this issue, comment "I'll take this".

items.title: Record MCP changes so they can be undone

labels.name: safety
labels.description: Part of making Shim the safest WordPress MCP plugin

items.body:
## Problem

Post revisions are the only way back from an MCP edit, and they cover post content only. A bad option update, term rename, menu change, user edit or plugin deactivation made by a client has no undo, and the site owner has to work out by hand what changed.

Elsewhere: Royal MCP returns undo tokens valid for 72 hours. Cowboy MCP keeps an undo journal plus database checkpoints. Flex MCP has per-change and per-session undo and redo. Easy MCP AI keeps a change history with diff and apply.

## Scope

- Before a write ability runs, snapshot the state it is about to change: post fields and meta, option value, term, menu and menu items, user fields (never passwords), plugin activation state.
- Return a change ID in the ability result, so the client can offer "undo that".
- `shim-mcp/changes-list` and `shim-mcp/changes-undo`, plus a list in Tools > Shim MCP with an Undo button.
- Undo refuses when the object has changed since, unless the caller confirms, and needs the same capability as the original write.
- Retention setting, default 7 days, pruned by cron. Reuse the storage from #57 and hook in through the filters from #53.
- Permanent deletes stay out of scope unless the object was snapshotted first. Trashed posts already restore through core.

## Done when

- Undo restores post, meta, option, term, menu, user and plugin-state changes made over MCP.
- Undo of an object edited since is refused with a clear message.
- A user without the original capability cannot undo.
- Tests cover each object type and the conflict case.

items.title: Support MCP 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28
items.body:
## Problem

Shim negotiates 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05 only ([`InitializeHandler.php#L23-L27`](https://github.com/justadityaraj/shim-mcp/blob/v1.1.0/includes/Server/Handlers/Initialize/InitializeHandler.php#L23-L27)). The current revision is 2026-07-28. MCP Adapter 0.7.x serves 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28, and so do Easy MCP AI, Royal MCP, Flex MCP, Agent Abilities for MCP, AcrossAI and Albert. Clients fall back to 2025-06-18 today; as they drop older revisions, Shim stops connecting.

## What changed

- **2025-11-25:** icons on tools, resources and prompts; URL-mode elicitation; Client ID Metadata Documents for authorization; 403 on an invalid `Origin` (see #51).
- **2026-07-28:** sessionless `server/discover`; request `_meta`; `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers; `resultType`; `subscriptions/listen`; error codes -32020 to -32022.

## Approach

`includes/Server/` is derived from MCP Adapter and the project keeps it close to upstream. Upstream 0.7.x already implements both revisions, so port from it rather than writing a new implementation: diff upstream 0.6.2 (whose session safeguards Shim carries) against 0.7.1, bring the protocol changes across, keep the `ShimMcp` namespace and the stdio bridge. Upstream 0.7 also restructured init, so coordinate with #49.

## Done when

- `initialize` with 2025-11-25 or 2026-07-28 negotiates that revision, and the older three still work.
- `server/discover` answers without a session.
- readme.txt lists every supported revision. It mentions only 2025-06-18 today.
- E2E tests run the handshake and a tool call on each supported revision over both transports.

items.body:
## Description

Developers increasingly ask AI assistants how to call a contract. A Model Context Protocol server exposing SoroVault's search, interfaces and generated clients lets those assistants answer from the registry instead of guessing.

## Requirements and context

High complexity (200 points): a substantial piece of work with design decisions. **Comment with your intended approach before writing code**, so the design can be agreed first.

- Repository: `soroworks/sorovault`
- Contributor setup: `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- Primary files: `internal/mcp/`, `cmd/sorovault/`

## Suggested execution

1. Comment on this issue to be assigned before you start, so two people don't duplicate the work.
2. Fork the repository and create a branch: `git checkout -b mcp-server`
3. Post your intended approach as a comment and wait for agreement.
4. Read the primary files, then implement as described under **Implementation guidance**.
5. Run the commands under **Testing**, then open a PR against `main` that says `Closes #<this issue>`.

## What "done" looks like

- `sorovault mcp` serves MCP tools for searching contracts, fetching an interface or function, and generating a client.
- It works against a local store or a remote SoroVault API.
- It is read-only, with tests for each tool.

## Implementation guidance

Comment with your design first; use the official MCP Go SDK if available.

## Testing

```
make check
```

`make check` runs `go vet`, the gofmt check and the full test suite; none of it needs a network. To include the Postgres store suite, run `make test-all` (it uses `TEST_DATABASE_URL`), as CI does. If you add or change an HTTP route, update `internal/api/openapi.json` — `TestOpenAPICoversEveryRoute` will fail until you do.

items.title: Two MCP agents waiting at once both receive the same change
items.body:
**Labels:** `enhancement`, `help wanted`

`docs/agent-handoff.md` tells agents there is one waiter at a time. Changes are not claimed, so two agents blocked in `wait_for_change` both receive the same change and can both apply it.

That is pinned on purpose. `test/mcp-handoff-cases.mjs` ("two waiters are both handed the same change") says a lease, if one is ever added, has to change that test rather than drift past it. The tool description says the same thing to the model.

A lease would let the second waiter skip a change the first one has taken, and return it if that agent disconnects without `resolve_change`. Until then the documented workaround stands: one waiting agent.

items.title: Examples: use the MCP server from Python agent frameworks
items.body:
**Why:** people building their own agents can give them pubchem-finder's 17 tools through MCP, without touching the Python API. A small `examples/` folder would show how, one short runnable script per framework. Part of #23.

**Proposal:** add `examples/` with scripts like these. One framework per PR is fine.
- **Plain MCP Python client:** `stdio_client` + `ClientSession`, list the tools, call `compound_properties` and `similarity_search`. [`scripts/smoke.py`](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/blob/master/scripts/smoke.py) and [`tests/e2e/test_stdio.py`](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/blob/master/tests/e2e/test_stdio.py) already do this and are a good starting point. It needs no API key, so CI could run it.
- **OpenAI Agents SDK** with `MCPServerStdio` ([docs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/mcp/)).
- **LangChain / LangGraph** with [`langchain-mcp-adapters`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-mcp-adapters) (`MultiServerMCPClient`, stdio).
- Others welcome: PydanticAI, LlamaIndex, the Claude Agent SDK...

**Conventions**
- Each script is short (well under 100 lines) and declares its own dependencies with [inline script metadata](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/scripts/#declaring-script-dependencies), so `uv run examples/<name>.py` just works and the framework stays out of pubchem-finder's dependencies.
- Start the server with `command="uvx", args=["pubchem-finder", "mcp"]`.
- Ask one realistic question, e.g. *"Find close analogues of aspirin in the local index and summarise what changed"* (needs `uvx pubchem-finder index build --limit 1`), or a PubChem lookup that needs no index.
- Read API keys from the environment, and say which one at the top of the file.
- Link the folder from the README's "Use it from Python" section.

**Done when** at least one framework example runs as described, with the exact command and its output in the PR.

items.title: Serve MCP over Streamable HTTP for web-based and shared setups
items.body:
**Why:** `pubchem-finder mcp` only speaks stdio, so it needs a client that can launch a local process. Two cases need a URL instead:
- clients that only connect to remote servers, such as web-based chat apps and their connectors;
- shared setups, such as one machine holding the full PubChem index (tens of GB) for a team.

The MCP Python SDK already ships the Streamable HTTP transport. `MCPServer.run()` accepts `transport="streamable-http"`, so most of the work is the command-line options, safe defaults, a test and docs. Part of #23.

**Proposal**
- `pubchem-finder mcp --transport http [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 8000]`. stdio stays the default, so existing setups don't change.
- Bind to `127.0.0.1` by default. Binding elsewhere needs an explicit `--host`, and the docs should say:
  - to put HTTPS and authentication in front, for example a reverse proxy;
  - that every user's PubChem requests then come from one IP, so they share PubChem's limit of 5 requests per second.
- **Test:** an e2e test that starts the server on a free port and runs the MCP client over Streamable HTTP, like [`tests/e2e/test_stdio.py`](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/blob/master/tests/e2e/test_stdio.py). It should pass on Linux, macOS and Windows CI.
- **Docs:** an "Over HTTP" section in [docs/clients.md](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/blob/master/docs/clients.md) and a line in the README.

**Pointers**
- [`src/pubchem_finder/mcp_server.py`](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/blob/master/src/pubchem_finder/mcp_server.py): `main()` calls `mcp.run(transport="stdio")`.
- [`src/pubchem_finder/cli.py`](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/blob/master/src/pubchem_finder/cli.py): the `mcp` command.
- The tools already run their blocking work on worker threads. On-disk index search deliberately stays single-process (see `LocalIndex.search`), which matters more once several clients share one server.

**Out of scope for this issue:** built-in OAuth, and a Docker image (worth its own issue once HTTP exists).

items.title: Support MCP clients beyond Claude
items.body:
pubchem-finder's MCP server speaks standard MCP over stdio, so any client that can launch a local MCP server should be able to run it with the same command (`uvx pubchem-finder mcp`). So far only **Claude Code** and **Claude Desktop** are documented.

This issue tracks a tested setup for each popular client. Each one is a sub-issue below and a good first contribution: no Python needed, just a client you already use and about half an hour.

**How to help**
1. Pick a client from the sub-issues and comment that you're on it.
2. Follow [docs/clients.md](https://github.com/MysterionRise/pubchem-finder/blob/master/docs/clients.md) (added in #22). It covers:
   - the settings,
   - four questions that check the setup end to end,
   - the format for a new section.
3. Open a PR that adds your section and updates the table.

**Using a client that isn't listed** (Continue, Goose, Amazon Q, Warp, Roo Code...)? Open an issue or a PR in the same format. It's just as welcome.

The two `enhancement` sub-issues need code:
- an HTTP transport, for web-based clients that can't launch local processes;
- examples for agent frameworks.
